**Resubmitted: deviation (fallback target), confidence 0.78.** Redline validated `ok:true` with the minimality gate passing.

Repair made in response to the verifier's deterministic failure ("Customer convenience termination present"):

1. **Operation 1 (insert after p0079)** — adds one sentence to Section 14 making our right explicit: *"Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon written notice to TrueLink."* This removes the ambiguity that Section 14 is merely a wind-down timing provision, while the retained sentence continues to supply the effective-date mechanic (last day of the month following notice), which is more favourable to us than the fallback's 60–90 days. Insert (rather than replace) was used because every in-place variant exceeded the 1.5× word ratio.
2. **Operation 2 (replace in p0078)** — unchanged from the accepted version: TrueLink's non-renewal notice becomes ninety (90) days, curing the walk-away trigger, with our 30-day notice preserved verbatim.

Element coverage: elements 1 and 4 addressed by operations 1 and 2; the fee-cap element is already met (no early-termination fee or penalty exists) and the end-of-term-only limit on TrueLink's exit is already met, both with verbatim quotes from retained text. Preferred-level items (30-day notice, pro-rata refund) are noted in the rationale only, as fees are invoiced monthly in arrears.
